newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Perky Australian bills help bonds pare fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Perky Australian bills help bonds pare fall.

text.p: Australian bill futures rallied strongly as talk centred on next week's Reserve Bank board meeting, which helped to lift a bond market that had been weighed down by weak U.S. Treasuries initially.

Analysts said some major banks were seen active in the market as they protectively took positions amid talk that the central bank will ease policy for the second consecutive meeting after generally taking the market by surprise in July.
"A lot of people missed out on the last move, and they just don't want to miss out again," one trader said.
The RBA cut rate by 50 basis points to 7.0 percent in July.

The active December 90-day bill futures contract rallied to 93.33, indicating a cash rate of 6.67 percent at maturity, having dipped to 93.21 in early trading following a weak U.S. market where talk continues of a Fed tightening.

Reuters monthly interest rate poll showed economists generally expecting the next move in interest rates to be down, although none clearly expected the RBA to loosen policy after the September meeting.
Bonds perked up from the U.S.-led lows amid the RBA talk and on rumours of a dual currency samurai bond issue being fixed, but 10-year bond yields remained pegged just above 8.0 percent.

The local yield curve also steepened on the rate cut talk with the short-end outperforming, while spreads to the U.S. and Canada reversed an early widening. Meanwhile, New Zealand bonds drifted higher in subdued trade. The U.S. bond market has a shortened session today ahead of Monday's Labor Day holiday.
